B05-Q003.explanation: A conditional receipt makes coverage effective on the date of application OR the date of the required medical examination, whichever occurs later, provided the applicant is insurable at standard rates. Because the applicant died before receiving the required medical examination, the condition for coverage was never met. The insurer will deny the claim and return the premium.

optionExplanations.It will pay the full death benefit, beca: Paying the premium is only a condition; completing required medical exams is another. Coverage does not begin until all requirements are met.
optionExplanations.It will pay the death benefit, but will: Insurers do not pay claims with deductions for unmet underwriting requirements. If the requirements are not met, there is no coverage.
optionExplanations.It will deny the claim, because conditio: Conditional receipts can cover accidental death, provided the applicant has met all conditions (including medical examination) and is determined to be insurable.

B05-Q015.question: A policyholder purchases an individual health insurance policy and chooses to pay premiums weekly. Under the Uniform Individual Accident and Sickness Policy Provisions Law, what is the mandatory grace period for this policy?
options: 7 days
10 days
30 days
31 days
B05-Q015.explanation: In individual health insurance, the grace period is linked to the method of payment of the premium. The mandatory grace period is 7 days for policies with weekly premiums, 10 days for policies with monthly premiums and 31 days for all other modes (quarterly, semi-annual, annual).

optionExplanations.10 days: 10 days is the grace period required if premiums are paid monthly.
optionExplanations.30 days: 30 days is a common term in insurance, but grace periods for health policies are 7, 10 or 31 days.
optionExplanations.31 days: 31 days is the grace period for policies where premiums are paid quarterly, semi-annually or annually, as well as for life insurance policies.

B05-Q005.question: A self-employed architect purchases an individual Disability Income policy and pays the premiums from her personal after-tax savings. How are premiums and benefits treated for federal income tax purposes?
options: Premiums are tax deductible; Profits are taxable as income.
Premiums are not tax deductible; Profits are received tax-free.
Premiums are tax deductible; Profits are received tax-free.
Premiums are not tax deductible; Profits are taxable as income.
B05-Q005.correctAnswer: Premiums are not tax deductible; Profits are received tax-free.
B05-Q005.explanation: For a individually owned disability income policy where the insured pays the premiums with after-tax dollars, the premiums are not tax deductible. Consequently, if the insured becomes disabled, disability benefits are received 100% tax-free.

optionExplanations.Premiums are tax deductible; Profits are: This describes the tax treatment of group disability income insurance when the employer pays the premiums.
The IRS does not allow a person to deduct premiums and also receive benefits tax-free.
optionExplanations.Premiums are not tax deductible; Profits: Since the premiums were paid with after-tax dollars, the benefits are not taxed again.

B05-Q014.question: Under the mandatory “Time Limit on Certain Defenses” provision included in all individual health insurance policies, how long does the insurer have to void the policy or deny a claim based on incorrect statements made on the application (excluding fraudulent statements)?
options: 1 year
2 years
3 years
There is no time limit; incorrect statements can always void the policy
B05-Q014.explanation: The Time Limit on Certain Defenses provision (similar to the incontestability clause in life insurance) states that after the policy has been in force for 2 years, no misstatements on the application, except fraudulent ones, can be used to void the policy or deny a claim.

optionExplanations.1 year: 1 year is the limit for taking legal action against an insurer after presenting proof of loss (in some cases), but the contestability period is 2 years.
optionExplanations.3 years: 3 years is the time limit for defending claims on some older life insurance policies from other eras, but the standard uniform health provision is strictly 2 years.
optionExplanations.There is no time limit; incorrect statem: Although fraudulent claims can often be challenged at any time in health insurance, non-fraudulent claims are protected after 2 years.

B05-Q009.question: A small business owner purchases a Business Overhead Expense (BOE) disability policy to keep the business running if he or she suffers a disabling injury. Which of the following expenses would NOT be covered by BOE policy benefits?
options: Utility Bills and Property Taxes
Employee salaries and payroll taxes
The personal salary of the business owner
Rent of commercial premises
B05-Q009.correctAnswer: The personal salary of the business owner
B05-Q009.explanation: Business Overhead Expense (BOE) insurance is designed to pay for the routine, ongoing operating expenses of a business if the owner becomes disabled. Covers rent, utilities and employee salaries. It specifically DOES NOT cover the disabled owner's personal salary, income or profit.

optionExplanations.Utility Bills and Property Taxes: Utilities and property taxes are standard fixed operating expenses covered by a BOE policy.
optionExplanations.Employee salaries and payroll taxes: Employee wages (excluding disabled owner) are critical ongoing expenses covered by BOE.
optionExplanations.Rent of commercial premises: Commercial premises rent is a classic example of an operating expense covered by a BOE policy.

B05-Q010.question: Two equal partners own a successful restaurant. They want to ensure that if one of the partners dies, the surviving partner has the funds to buy out the deceased partner's share of the business from the heirs. To accomplish this, each partner purchases a life insurance policy on the other. This arrangement is known as:
options: A Cross-Purchase Buy-Sell Agreement
An Entity Purchase Buy-Sell Agreement
Executive Bonus Plan
Key Person Insurance
B05-Q010.explanation: In a Cross-Purchase Buy-Sell Agreement, individual business owners purchase life insurance policies from each other. When one dies, the survivor receives the death benefit and uses it to buy out the deceased owner's interest in the business.

optionExplanations.An Entity Purchase Buy-Sell Agreement: In an Entity Purchase (or Stock Redemption) plan, the business itself purchases the policies on the owners, pays the premiums and buys out the deceased owner's interest.
optionExplanations.Executive Bonus Plan: An Executive Bonus Plan is an additional benefit where an employer pays the premium for a personal life insurance policy owned by an employee.
optionExplanations.Key Person Insurance: Key Person Insurance is used to protect the business against financial loss due to the death of a critical employee, not to facilitate the transfer of ownership of the business.

B05-Q004.question: A corporation purchases a Key Person life insurance policy on its top executive. The corporation is the applicant, policyholder, premium payer and beneficiary. Who must sign the application to consent to the issuance of this policy?
options: Only an authorized officer of the corporation
Only the Key Person (the executive)
Both an authorized officer of the corporation and the Key Person
The board of directors of the corporation and the agent
B05-Q004.correctAnswer: Both an authorized officer of the corporation and the Key Person
B05-Q004.explanation: In any life insurance transaction involving third-party ownership, both the applicant/holder (an authorized officer of the corporation) and the proposed insured (the Key Person) must sign the application. The insured must sign to give written consent to be insured.

optionExplanations.Only an authorized officer of the corpor: The corporation cannot legally purchase a life insurance policy on an employee without the employee's written consent and signature.
optionExplanations.Only the Key Person (the executive): The executive must sign as the insured, but the corporation must also sign as the applicant and policyholder.
optionExplanations.The board of directors of the corporatio: Although the agent signs the application, the critical signature missing from this option is the consent of the proposed insured.

B05-Q017.question: When an employee terminates employment and loses coverage under a group life insurance policy, he or she typically has the right to convert the group coverage to an individual whole life policy without providing evidence of insurability. Under Texas law, what is the length of this conversion period?
options: 10 days
20 days
31 days
60 days
B05-Q017.explanation: The group life insurance conversion privilege gives the employee 31 days after termination of employment to convert their temporary group coverage to a permanent individual (whole life) policy without demonstrating insurability.

optionExplanations.10 days: 10 days is the standard free look period for life insurance.
optionExplanations.20 days: 20 days is the standard notice of claim requirement for health insurance, and the free look period for replacement life policies.
optionExplanations.60 days: 60 days is the conversion window for some health insurance policies, but group life conversion is strictly 31 days.

B05-Q019.question: An employee participates in an employer-sponsored 401(k) qualified retirement plan. The employer matches the employee's contributions up to 5%. When are employer contributions and investment earnings on those contributions taxed to the employee?
options: They are taxed in the year in which the contribution is made.
They are taxed annually based on account growth.
They are taxed as ordinary income when distributed or withdrawn.
They are completely tax-free to the employee at the time of distribution.
B05-Q019.correctAnswer: They are taxed as ordinary income when distributed or withdrawn.
B05-Q019.explanation: In a qualified retirement plan like a 401(k), employer contributions are deductible to the employer and grow tax deferred in the account. They are not taxed to the employee until the funds are distributed or withdrawn, at which time the entire withdrawal (contributions and earnings) is taxed as ordinary income.

optionExplanations.They are taxed in the year in which the: This describes non-qualified compensation. Contributions to qualified plans are deferred and not taxed in the year they are made.
optionExplanations.They are taxed annually based on account: Qualified plans enjoy tax-deferred growth. Profits are not taxed annually.
optionExplanations.They are completely tax-free to the empl: Distributions from traditional qualified plans are fully taxable as ordinary income. Only Roth accounts (funded with after-tax dollars) offer tax-free distributions.

B05-Q023.question: Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) offer important tax advantages for people enrolled in High Deductible Health Plans (HDHPs). Which of the following best describes the tax treatment of HSA withdrawals used for qualified medical expenses?
options: They are taxed as ordinary income, but are not subject to a penalty.
They are taxed as capital gains.
They are completely tax free.
They are tax-free only up to the amount of the plan's deductible.
B05-Q023.explanation: The main advantage of a Health Savings Account (HSA) is its triple tax benefit: contributions are tax deductible, earnings grow tax deferred, and withdrawals used for qualified medical expenses are completely tax-free.

optionExplanations.They are taxed as ordinary income, but a: If an HSA withdrawal is used for NON-qualified expenses before age 65, it is taxed as ordinary income AND is subject to a 20% penalty.
HSA funds are never taxed as capital gains; They are tax-free (for medical expenses) or taxed as ordinary income (for non-medical expenses).
optionExplanations.They are tax-free only up to the amount: Tax-free withdrawals are not limited by the deductible; apply to all qualified medical expenses, including copays, coinsurance, and dental/vision care.

B05-Q024.question: Under the mandatory “Entire Contract” provision found in all individual health insurance policies, the entire contract consists of the policy document, any accompanying rider or endorsement, and what other important document?
options: Agent sales illustration
The Medical Information Bureau (MIB) report
A copy of the original application
The treating doctor's statement
B05-Q024.correctAnswer: A copy of the original application
B05-Q024.explanation: The Entire Contract provision states that the health insurance policy, including any rider, endorsement and a copy of the original application, constitutes the entire contract between the parties. Nothing outside of these attached documents can be used in court to alter the terms.

optionExplanations.Agent sales illustration: Sales illustrations are marketing materials and are explicitly not part of the legal contract.
optionExplanations.The Medical Information Bureau (MIB) rep: The MIB report is an underwriting tool used by the insurer, but is not attached to or part of the legal contract.
optionExplanations.The treating doctor's statement: Physician statements are evidence of underwriting, but unless incorporated into the application itself, they are not part of the entire contract.

B05-Q022.question: Which part of the Original Medicare program primarily covers inpatient hospital care, skilled nursing facility care, and hospice care?
options: Medicare Part A
Medicare Part B
Medicare Part C
Medicare Part D
B05-Q022.explanation: Medicare Part A is hospital insurance. Covers inpatient hospital care, skilled nursing facility care, hospice care, and some home health services.

optionExplanations.Medicare Part B: Medicare Part B is health insurance, which primarily covers medical services, outpatient care, medical supplies, and preventive services.
optionExplanations.Medicare Part C: Medicare Part C (Medicare Advantage) is a private plan option that bundles Part A, Part B, and usually Part D into a single plan.
optionExplanations.Medicare Part D: Medicare Part D is the prescription drug coverage program.

B06-Q004.question: When an applicant is purchasing an individual disability income policy, how does his or her choice of elimination period affect the policy premium?
options: A longer elimination period results in a higher premium.
A longer elimination period results in a lower premium.
The elimination period affects only the benefit amount, not the premium.
A shorter elimination period reduces the premium because the insurer pays fewer claims in the long run.
B06-Q004.correctAnswer: A longer elimination period results in a lower premium.
B06-Q004.explanation: The elimination period (waiting period) works like a time deductible. A longer elimination period means the insured takes on more short-term risk, which reduces the insurer's liability and therefore lowers the cost of the premium.

optionExplanations.A longer elimination period results in a: This is an inverse relationship. Waiting longer makes the policy cheaper, not more expensive.
optionExplanations.The elimination period affects only the: The elimination period directly impacts the cost of the premium.
optionExplanations.A shorter elimination period reduces the: A shorter elimination period increases the premium because the insurer must begin paying benefits sooner.

B06-Q002.question: Three years after issuing a whole life insurance policy, the insurer discovers that the insured intentionally concealed a severe medical diagnosis in the original application. The insured dies shortly after this discovery. How should the insurer handle the claim?
options: Deny the claim and return the premiums, because intentional concealment constitutes fraud.
Deny the claim but withhold premiums due to the applicant's fraudulent act.
Pay the full death benefit because the incontestability period has expired.
Pay a reduced benefit based on what the premiums would have bought if the true medical history had been known.
B06-Q002.correctAnswer: Pay the full death benefit because the incontestability period has expired.
B06-Q002.explanation: The incontestability clause in a life insurance policy prevents the insurer from denying a claim due to material misrepresentations on the application after the policy has been in force for 2 years. Unlike health insurance, life insurance cannot be challenged even for fraud after the 2-year period has passed.

optionExplanations.Deny the claim and return the premiums,: In life insurance, even intentional fraud cannot be used to void the policy after the 2-year incontestability period.
optionExplanations.Deny the claim but withhold premiums due: The insurer cannot deny the claim after 2 years.
optionExplanations.Pay a reduced benefit based on what the: This describes the provision for misreporting age or sex, not the remedy for general medical concealment.

B06-Q005.question: To avoid a 10% IRS tax penalty for premature distributions from a qualified retirement plan or traditional IRA, a person generally must wait until reaching what age to withdraw funds?
options: 55 years
59 1/2 years
62 years
65 years
B06-Q005.explanation: Distributions from qualified retirement plans and IRAs taken before the owner reaches age 59 1/2 are considered premature and are subject to a 10% tax penalty in addition to ordinary income taxes.

optionExplanations.55 years: The age of 55 is tied to a specific exception for 401(k) plans upon separation, not the general rule.
optionExplanations.62 years: Age 62 is the youngest age to receive standard Social Security retirement benefits.
optionExplanations.65 years: Age 65 is the eligibility age for Medicare, but retirement funds can be accessed without the 10% penalty starting at age 59 1/2.

B06-Q007.question: In an individual disability income policy, which definition of total disability is considered most favorable to the insured?
options: Any occupation
Own occupation
Presumptive disability
Partial disability
B06-Q007.explanation: The 'own occupation' definition for total disability is the most favorable and usually the most expensive. It defines disability as the inability to perform the functions of the insured's regular occupation, potentially allowing him or her to receive benefits even if he or she finds work in another field.

optionExplanations.Any occupation: The definition of 'any occupation' is more restrictive, paying benefits only if the insured is unable to perform the functions of any occupation for which he or she is reasonably prepared by education, training or experience.
optionExplanations.Presumptive disability: Presumptive disability specifies certain conditions (such as loss of two limbs or blindness) that automatically qualify for full benefits, but it is a provision rather than the core definition of general total disability.
optionExplanations.Partial disability: Partial disability pays a reduced benefit when the insured can still work part-time or perform some, but not all, of their duties.

B06-Q008.question: A married couple wants annuity income that continues as long as either spouse is alive, and that stops only after the second spouse dies. Which annuity payment option best matches that goal?
options: Life income with certain period
Joint and surviving life
Fixed amount
Cash Back Living
B06-Q008.explanation: A joint and surviving life option continues the income until the second annuitant dies. It is commonly used when spouses want lifetime income protection for both lives.

optionExplanations.Life income with certain period: Certain period living income guarantees payments for life, but if the annuitant dies early, the remaining payments of the certain period continue only until the end of that period, not necessarily until a second person dies.
optionExplanations.Fixed amount: A fixed-amount option pays a set amount until the funds are depleted, regardless of whether either spouse is still alive.
optionExplanations.Cash Back Living: A cash back life option provides a refund if total payments before death are less than the premium paid, but is not designed to continue lifetime income for a surviving spouse.

B06-Q009.question: If a permanent life insurance policy becomes overfunded and fails to meet the IRS 7-payment test, it is classified as a Modified Endowment Contract (MEC). How are cash withdrawals from an MEC treated for tax purposes?
options: They are tax-free because they are considered a return of capital.
They are taxed under the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) method.
They are taxed under the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) method, meaning profits are withdrawn and taxed first.
They are taxed as long-term capital gains.
B06-Q009.correctAnswer: They are taxed under the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) method, meaning profits are withdrawn and taxed first.
B06-Q009.explanation: Once a policy is classified as an MEC, it loses the favorable FIFO tax treatment of standard life insurance. Withdrawals from an MEC are taxed under the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) method, meaning the taxable interest/earnings are considered withdrawn first. Additionally, withdrawals before age 59 1/2 are subject to a 10% penalty.

optionExplanations.They are tax-free because they are consi: Withdrawals from an MEC are not tax-free until all earnings have been withdrawn and taxed.
optionExplanations.They are taxed under the First-In, First: FIFO is the favorable tax treatment for non-MEC standard life insurance policies.
optionExplanations.They are taxed as long-term capital gain: Earnings withdrawn from an MEC are taxed as ordinary income, not capital gains.

B06-Q012.question: A Medicare beneficiary purchases a Medicare SELECT policy to save on premiums. For non-emergency care under this type of Medigap policy, which statement is generally true?
options: The policy pays full supplemental benefits regardless of which hospital or doctor the insured uses.
The insured generally must use network hospitals and, in some cases, network doctors to receive full benefits.
The policy works only if the insured enrolls in Medicare Advantage instead of Original Medicare.
The policy may deny emergency and non-emergency claims as long as services are received out of network.
B06-Q012.correctAnswer: The insured generally must use network hospitals and, in some cases, network doctors to receive full benefits.
B06-Q012.explanation: Medicare SELECT is a Medigap policy with network restrictions. For non-emergency services, the insured must generally use network hospitals and sometimes network doctors to receive full supplemental benefits.

optionExplanations.The policy pays full supplemental benefi: That more closely describes a standard Medigap policy than a Medicare SELECT policy, which adds network restrictions.
optionExplanations.The policy works only if the insured enr: Medicare SELECT remains a form of Medigap, supplementing Original Medicare rather than replacing it with Medicare Advantage.
optionExplanations.The policy may deny emergency and non-em: Emergency services are the key exception. Network restrictions generally apply to non-emergency care, not actual emergencies.

B06-Q011.question: A policyholder takes out a loan against the cash value of his or her whole life insurance. Over time, the policyholder does not pay the annual interest on the loan. What happens to the policy if unpaid interest causes the total loan balance to exceed the available cash surrender value of the policy?
options: The policy will be converted to an extended term policy.
The insurer will garnish the policyholder's wages to pay off the loan.
The policy will expire and terminate, generally after a 30-day notice period.
The death benefit will be reduced, but the policy will remain in force indefinitely.
B06-Q011.correctAnswer: The policy will expire and terminate, generally after a 30-day notice period.
B06-Q011.explanation: If a policy loan is not paid, the unpaid interest is added to the principal. If the total outstanding loan balance (principal plus interest) ever equals or exceeds the cash value of the policy, the policy will lapse and terminate. Insurers must provide at least 30 days written notice before the policy is voided.

optionExplanations.The policy will be converted to an exten: Extended term is a non-forfeiture option used when the policyholder stops paying premiums while cash value still exists, not when a loan exceeds cash value.
optionExplanations.The insurer will garnish the policyholde: Policy loans are essentially advances on the policy funds themselves; There is no legal obligation to pay them, so an insurer cannot garnish wages.
optionExplanations.The death benefit will be reduced, but t: The policy cannot remain in force if there is no cash value left to support it against the loan.

B06-Q013.question: The owner of a life insurance policy adds a guaranteed insurability endorsement to his or her policy. What is the main benefit of this endorsement?
options: Prevents the policy from lapse if the insured becomes permanently disabled.
Allows the policyholder to purchase additional coverage at specified future dates without providing evidence of insurability.
It guarantees that the premium will never increase during the life of the policy.
Pays double the face amount if the insured dies in an accident.
B06-Q013.correctAnswer: Allows the policyholder to purchase additional coverage at specified future dates without providing evidence of insurability.
B06-Q013.explanation: The guaranteed insurability endorsement allows the policyholder to purchase additional amounts of life insurance at specific ages or life events (such as marriage or birth of a child) at standard rates, without the need to prove insurability (no medical exams or health questions).

optionExplanations.Prevents the policy from lapse if the in: This describes the premium waiver endorsement.
optionExplanations.It guarantees that the premium will neve: Premiums for whole life policies are already guaranteed at a fixed level. The endorsement itself does not guarantee the cost of *additional* coverage; The new coverage is calculated according to the reached age of the insured.
optionExplanations.Pays double the face amount if the insur: This describes the accidental death benefit (double indemnity) endorsement.

B06-Q010.question: Under Texas insurance law, an insurer is strictly prohibited from charging different premiums or denying coverage to persons of the same actuarial class based solely on which of the following characteristics?
options: Age
tobacco use
Blindness or partial blindness
History of severe heart disease
B06-Q010.explanation: The Texas Insurance Code strictly prohibits insurers from refusing to insure, refusing to continue insuring, or limiting the coverage available to a person based solely on blindness or partial blindness, classifying it as unfair discrimination.

optionExplanations.Age: Age is a primary and legally permitted actuarial factor used to determine life and health premiums.
optionExplanations.tobacco use: Tobacco use carries known risks of morbidity and mortality and is a legally permitted charging factor.
optionExplanations.History of severe heart disease: Severe heart disease represents a distinct actuarial risk, and insurers can legally underwrite, classify or deny coverage based on that adverse medical history.

B06-Q014.question: An HSA owner is 67 years old and withdraws money from the Health Savings Account for a non-medical expense. How is that distribution generally treated for federal tax purposes?
options: It is completely tax free because the owner is over 65 years old.
It is taxable as ordinary income, but the 20% penalty does not apply.
It is taxable as ordinary income and is also subject to a 20% penalty.
It is taxed as long-term capital gain.
B06-Q014.correctAnswer: It is taxable as ordinary income, but the 20% penalty does not apply.
B06-Q014.explanation: After age 65, HSA distributions used for nonqualified expenses remain taxable as ordinary income, but the additional 20% penalty no longer applies.

optionExplanations.It is completely tax free because the ow: Only HSA distributions used for qualified medical expenses are tax-free.
optionExplanations.It is taxable as ordinary income and is: The additional 20% tax applies to non-qualified HSA distributions before age 65, not after age 65.
Non-qualified HSA distributions are not taxed as capital gains.

B06-Q015.question: A parent purchases a youth whole life policy for his 10-year-old son and adds a payer benefit endorsement. What protection does this endorsement provide?
options: Doubles the death benefit if the child dies before age 21.
Waives premiums on the child's policy if the parent paying the premiums dies or becomes disabled.
It ensures that the child can purchase any amount of insurance at age 18 without evidence of insurability.
Returns all premiums if the child survives to age 21.
B06-Q015.correctAnswer: Waives premiums on the child's policy if the parent paying the premiums dies or becomes disabled.
B06-Q015.explanation: A payer benefit endorsement is commonly used on youth policies. If the parent paying the premiums dies or becomes disabled, the insurer waives future premiums so the child's coverage can remain in effect.

optionExplanations.Doubles the death benefit if the child d: That describes an accidental death or other special benefit, not a payer benefit endorsement.
optionExplanations.It ensures that the child can purchase a: That describes a concept of guaranteed insurability, not the payer's endorsement of benefit.
optionExplanations.Returns all premiums if the child surviv: That describes a return of premium feature, not the payer's benefit endorsement.

B06-Q017.question: An insured purchased an individual accident and health policy while working as an accountant. A year later, the insured changed jobs and became a commercial roofer, but never notified the insurer. Under the Change of Occupation provision, what can happen if the insured is later injured on the job?
options: The claim must be paid in full because occupation changes never affect accident and health benefits after issuance.
The insurer may reduce benefits to the amount that the premium paid would have bought for the more dangerous occupation.
The insurer can void the policy entirely for concealment, even if the change of occupancy provision applies.
The insurer must return all premiums and deny the claim because the insured switched to a hazardous occupation.
B06-Q017.correctAnswer: The insurer may reduce benefits to the amount that the premium paid would have bought for the more dangerous occupation.
B06-Q017.explanation: Under the Change of Occupation provision, if the insured changes to a more dangerous occupation, the insurer may reduce the benefit to what the premium paid would have purchased for that more dangerous class.

optionExplanations.The claim must be paid in full because o: The standard provision exists precisely because changes in occupation can affect accident and health benefits.
optionExplanations.The insurer can void the policy entirely: The Change of Occupation provision provides a method of adjustment rather than automatically voiding the contract.
optionExplanations.The insurer must return all premiums and: The standard outcome is benefit adjustment, not automatic return of premiums and claim denial.

B06-Q021.question: An applicant applies for a life insurance policy but does not pay the initial premium at the time of application. When the agent subsequently delivers the approved policy, what must the agent charge in addition to the initial premium to put the policy into effect?
options: A signed conditional receipt
A signed Declaration of Good Health
A new medical examination report
An inspection report fee
B06-Q021.correctAnswer: A signed Declaration of Good Health
B06-Q021.explanation: If the initial premium is not paid with the application, coverage may not take effect immediately. Upon delivery of the policy, the agent must collect the premium and a Declaration of Good Health signed by the applicant, verifying that their health has not changed since the application was completed.

optionExplanations.A signed conditional receipt: A conditional receipt is provided when the premium IS collected at the time of application, not at the time of delivery.
optionExplanations.A new medical examination report: A new medical examination is not required unless the Declaration of Good Health reveals a change in condition.
optionExplanations.An inspection report fee: Inspection reports are requested by the subscriber during the application process, not collected as a fee upon delivery.

B06-Q019.question: What type of life insurance policy is most commonly marketed and used to provide funds to pay off the outstanding balance of a mortgage in the event of the premature death of the insured?
options: Temporary leveled life
Decreasing time life
Variable whole life
Whole life of single cousin
B06-Q019.explanation: Decreasing term life insurance has a death benefit that gradually decreases over the policy term, while the premium remains level. As the balance of a mortgage also decreases over time, this product is perfectly suited for mortgage protection.

optionExplanations.Temporary leveled life: Level term life maintains the same death benefit throughout the term; it does not follow a decreasing debt.
optionExplanations.Variable whole life: Variable whole life is a permanent investment-driven policy, not specifically designed to reflect declining debt.
optionExplanations.Whole life of single cousin: Single premium whole life requires a large upfront sum and provides level permanent coverage.

B06-Q020.question: If the owner of a participating whole life policy selects the 'paid additions' dividend option, how are the policy dividends used?
options: To reduce the next annual premium payment.
To purchase permanent single premium additions to the face amount of the policy.
To purchase a 1-year term life insurance endorsement.
To pay an outstanding policy loan.
B06-Q020.correctAnswer: To purchase permanent single premium additions to the face amount of the policy.
B06-Q020.explanation: Under the paid-up dividend option, the insurer uses the annual dividend as a single premium to purchase a small additional amount of fully paid-up whole life insurance. This increases both the total death benefit and the total cash value of the policy over time.

optionExplanations.To reduce the next annual premium paymen: This describes the premium reduction dividend option.
optionExplanations.To purchase a 1-year term life insurance: This describes the one-year term dividend option.
Although dividends can sometimes be applied to loan balances, that is not the definition of paid additions.

B06-Q022.question: In a basic hospital and surgical plan combined with a major medical supplemental policy, what is the primary purpose of the corridor deductible?
options: This is the annual deductible that must be met before the basic policy will pay any benefits.
It covers the gap between the benefits paid by the basic policy and the point at which major medical coverage begins to pay.
It limits the insured's out-of-pocket expenses during the year to a fixed maximum.
Allows the insured to use out-of-network providers with in-network cost-sharing levels.
B06-Q022.correctAnswer: It covers the gap between the benefits paid by the basic policy and the point at which major medical coverage begins to pay.
B06-Q022.explanation: A corridor deductible is used in supplemental arrangements for major medical expenses. It covers the gap between what the basic policy pays and when coverage for major medical expenses begins.

optionExplanations.This is the annual deductible that must: That describes the ordinary deductible under a basic policy, not the corridor deductible.
optionExplanations.It limits the insured's out-of-pocket ex: That describes a stop-loss or out-of-pocket maximum feature, not a runner deductible.
optionExplanations.Allows the insured to use out-of-network: That describes a network benefit design feature, not a supplemental major medical expense deductible concept.

B06-Q025.question: An insured becomes totally disabled and qualifies for the premium waiver endorsement on his or her life insurance policy. The endorsement has a standard waiting period of 6 months. What happens to premiums that are due during those first 6 months of disability?
options: The insurer automatically exempts them from the first day of disability.
The insured must pay them, but the insurer will reimburse them once the 6-month waiting period is over.
The insured does not have to pay them, but the unpaid amount is deducted from the death benefit.
The insured must pay them, and they are not reimbursed; The exemption only applies to premiums due after the sixth month.
B06-Q025.correctAnswer: The insured must pay them, but the insurer will reimburse them once the 6-month waiting period is over.
B06-Q025.explanation: Under the premium waiver endorsement, the insured must continue paying premiums during the waiting period (typically 6 months). If the insured remains totally disabled at the end of 6 months, the insurer begins to waive future premiums AND refund premiums paid during the waiting period.

optionExplanations.The insurer automatically exempts them f: Premiums are not waived immediately; The insured must first complete the waiting period.
optionExplanations.The insured does not have to pay them, b: Premiums are not deducted from the death benefit under this endorsement; are refunded.
optionExplanations.The insured must pay them, and they are: The waiver is retroactive to the onset of disability once the waiting period is met, meaning those initial premiums are refunded.

B06-Q023.question: How are death benefits from an individual life insurance policy generally treated for federal income tax purposes when paid in a lump sum to a named beneficiary?
options: They are taxed as long-term capital gains.
They are taxed as ordinary income for the beneficiary.
The beneficiary receives them completely free of income tax.
They are tax-free up to $100,000, and any excess is taxed as ordinary income.
B06-Q023.correctAnswer: The beneficiary receives them completely free of income tax.
B06-Q023.explanation: As a general rule under federal tax law, life insurance death benefits paid in a lump sum to a named beneficiary are received completely free of federal income tax.

optionExplanations.They are taxed as long-term capital gain: Death benefits are not subject to capital gains tax.
optionExplanations.They are taxed as ordinary income for th: Only interest earned on death benefits left with the insurer under a settlement option is taxed as ordinary income; The primary death benefit is tax-free.
optionExplanations.They are tax-free up to $100,000, and an: There is no legal limit on the amount of death benefit that can be received free of income tax.

B07-Q001.question: An insured submits a request for reinstatement and past due premium for an expired individual health insurance policy. The insurer issues a conditional receipt, but never formally notifies the insured in writing whether the request was approved or denied. Under standard health policy provisions, when is the policy automatically reinstated?
options: On the 15th day after the date of conditional receipt
The 30th day after the date of conditional receipt
On the 45th day after the date of conditional receipt
The policy cannot be reinstated without formal written approval from the insurer
B07-Q001.correctAnswer: On the 45th day after the date of conditional receipt
B07-Q001.explanation: Under the mandatory Reinstatement provision in individual health insurance, if the insurer requires a reinstatement application and issues a conditional receipt, the policy is automatically reinstated on the 45th day following the date of receipt, unless the insurer notifies the insured in writing of the denial before that date.

optionExplanations.On the 15th day after the date of condit: 15 days is too short and does not correspond to the uniform reinstatement provision.
optionExplanations.The 30th day after the date of condition: 30 days is a common time frame in insurance (e.g., grace periods), but the automatic reinstatement provision is specifically 45 days.
optionExplanations.The policy cannot be reinstated without: The uniform provision is designed to protect the insured from unreasonable delays by the insurer by imposing automatic reinstatement if a denial is not issued within 45 days.

B07-Q002.question: A corporation establishes an Executive Bonus plan to reward its vice president. The corporation purchases a whole life insurance policy in which the vice president is the policyholder and insured, and the corporation pays the premiums. How are these premium payments treated for tax purposes?
options: They are tax deductible for the corporation and tax free for the vice president.
They are tax deductible for the corporation and taxable as ordinary income for the vice president.
They are not tax deductible for the corporation, but are tax free for the vice president.
They are not tax deductible for the corporation, but the death benefit is taxable for the vice president's heirs.
B07-Q002.correctAnswer: They are tax deductible for the corporation and taxable as ordinary income for the vice president.
B07-Q002.explanation: In an Executive Bonus plan, the company pays the premium on a life insurance policy owned by the executive. The IRS treats these bonus payments as additional compensation to the executive. Therefore, the corporation can deduct the premiums as a business expense, and the executive must report the premium amounts as taxable ordinary income.

optionExplanations.They are tax deductible for the corporat: Bonuses are considered additional salary/compensation, so the executive cannot receive them tax-free.
optionExplanations.They are not tax deductible for the corp: The corporation can deduct the premiums because they are classified as employee compensation.
The premiums are tax deductible for the company, and the resulting death benefit paid to the executive's beneficiaries will generally be income tax free.

B07-Q003.question: Five years after issuing a whole life insurance policy, the insurer discovers during the investigation of a death claim that the insured declared an age 10 years younger on the application to obtain a lower premium. Although the 2-year incontestability period has long expired, how will the insurer handle the claim?
options: The insurer will deny the claim entirely because misreporting your age constitutes intentional fraud.
The insurer must pay the full original face amount because the incontestability period has passed.
The insurer will pay a reduced death benefit equal to the amount that the premium actually paid would have bought at the correct age.
The insurer will refund the premiums paid plus interest, but will deny the death benefit.
B07-Q003.correctAnswer: The insurer will pay a reduced death benefit equal to the amount that the premium actually paid would have bought at the correct age.
B07-Q003.explanation: The Incorrect Declaration of Age or Sex provision operates independently of the incontestability clause. If an incorrect statement of age or sex is discovered at any time, even decades after the policy is issued, the insurer adjusts the death benefit to the amount that the premium paid would have bought at the correct age. The policy is not canceled.

optionExplanations.The insurer will deny the claim entirely: Incorrect declaration of age does not void the policy; it only triggers an equitable adjustment of benefits.
optionExplanations.The insurer must pay the full original f: The incontestability clause expressly does not apply to incorrect statements of age or sex. The insurer can always adjust the benefit for age discrepancies.
optionExplanations.The insurer will refund the premiums pai: The insurer is obligated to pay the adjusted death benefit, not simply refund premiums.

B07-Q004.question: Under Section 1035 of the Internal Revenue Code, which of the following policy exchanges is strictly prohibited from receiving tax-free treatment?
options: Exchange a permanent life insurance policy for a deferred annuity.
Exchange a deferred annuity for a new permanent life insurance policy.
Exchange one deferred annuity for another deferred annuity.
Exchange a permanent life insurance policy for an endowment policy.
B07-Q004.correctAnswer: Exchange a deferred annuity for a new permanent life insurance policy.
B07-Q004.explanation: Section 1035 allows tax-free exchanges to prevent policyholders from being taxed when they simply update or change contracts. However, the IRS does not allow a person to exchange an annuity (which is fully taxable upon withdrawal) for a life insurance policy (which provides tax-free death benefits), because this would be an avenue to avoid taxation on the annuity earnings.

optionExplanations.Exchange a permanent life insurance poli: Exchanging life insurance for an annuity is permitted under Section 1035.
optionExplanations.Exchange one deferred annuity for anothe: Exchanging one annuity for another annuity is a standard and permitted 1035 exchange.
optionExplanations.Exchange a permanent life insurance poli: Exchanging life insurance for an endowment policy is permitted under Section 1035.

B07-Q007.question: What type of permanent life insurance policy is characterized by its unbundled structure, which allows the policyholder to flexibly adjust both the premium payment amounts and the death benefit (subject to insurability)?
options: traditional whole life
Variable whole life
universal life
Decreasing time life
B07-Q007.explanation: Universal life insurance (sometimes called flexible premium adjustable life) allows the policyholder to adjust premium payments and the face amount of the death benefit. The mortality charge, expense charges, and interest credited are itemized and clearly visible to the owner.

optionExplanations.traditional whole life: Traditional whole life has a fixed premium and a fixed death benefit that cannot be flexibly adjusted.
optionExplanations.Variable whole life: Variable whole life has a fixed premium, although the cash value fluctuates with market performance.
optionExplanations.Decreasing time life: Decreasing term life is a term policy with a decreasing face amount and no cash value component.

B07-Q008.question: An insured has an individual disability income policy that contains the standard optional 'Change of Occupation' provision. If the insured leaves their desk job for a significantly more dangerous occupation in construction and then files a claim, how will the insurer respond?
options: The insurer will deny the claim entirely because the change in occupation voided the policy.
The insurer will pay the original benefit amount, but will retroactively charge the insured for the higher premiums.
The insurer will pay reduced benefits equal to what the original premium would have bought for the more dangerous occupation.
The insurer will pay the full original benefit because the policy was already issued and in force.
B07-Q008.correctAnswer: The insurer will pay reduced benefits equal to what the original premium would have bought for the more dangerous occupation.
B07-Q008.explanation: Under the Change of Occupation provision, if an insured changes to a more dangerous job, the insurer will automatically adjust benefits downward. The new benefit amount will be what the premiums paid would have bought at the rates for the most dangerous occupation.

optionExplanations.The insurer will deny the claim entirely: A change in occupation does not void the policy; it only activates a benefit or premium adjustment.
optionExplanations.The insurer will pay the original benefi: The insurer does not issue retroactive invoices; adjusts the benefit amount payable to match the existing premium.
optionExplanations.The insurer will pay the full original b: If the policy contains this specific provision, the insurer has the legal right to reduce benefits to reflect the increased risk.

B07-Q010.question: An individual health insurance policy is issued with a 15-day trial period. What is the main purpose of this specific period?
options: Establish the time the insured must wait after a disability begins before receiving benefit payments.
Protect the insurer against adverse selection by excluding coverage for illnesses that occur shortly after the policy is issued.
Allow the insured time to review the policy and return it for a full refund of premium.
Define the period during which the insurer can challenge the validity of the contract due to fraud.
B07-Q010.correctAnswer: Protect the insurer against adverse selection by excluding coverage for illnesses that occur shortly after the policy is issued.
B07-Q010.explanation: The trial period is a one-time waiting period (often 15 or 30 days) immediately following the policy's effective date. During this time, illnesses are not covered, although accidental injuries are covered immediately. This protects the insurer from applicants who purchase coverage because they feel an illness is about to begin (adverse selection).

optionExplanations.Establish the time the insured must wait: This describes the Elimination Period, which kicks in after a covered loss occurs.
optionExplanations.Allow the insured time to review the pol: This describes the Free-Look period, a consumer protection feature.
optionExplanations.Define the period during which the insur: This describes the Time Limit provision on Certain Defenses (or Incontestability), which is typically 2 years.

B07-Q011.question: During the process of underwriting a life insurance policy, an insurer reviews the Medical Information Bureau (MIB). What is the main function of the MIB?
options: Provide insurers with access to an applicant's complete hospital and medical billing records.
Assign a required credit score used to determine life insurance premium rates.
Serve as a clearinghouse for encrypted medical information submitted by member insurers to help detect fraud and omissions in applications.
Perform independent physical examinations of applicants on behalf of the insurance company.
B07-Q011.correctAnswer: Serve as a clearinghouse for encrypted medical information submitted by member insurers to help detect fraud and omissions in applications.
B07-Q011.explanation: The Medical Information Bureau (MIB) is a nonprofit trade association that maintains confidential, encrypted medical information about people who have previously applied for life or health insurance. Helps subscribers detect inconsistencies, omissions and possible fraud by comparing current requests with previous reports.

optionExplanations.Provide insurers with access to an appli: The MIB does not have access to complete hospital records; is based on codes reported by member insurers from previous requests.
optionExplanations.Assign a required credit score used to d: The MIB does not issue credit scores. Financial data is typically obtained through a consumer reporting agency.
optionExplanations.Perform independent physical examination: The MIB does not perform physical examinations. The examinations are performed by paramedical professionals hired directly by the insurer.

B07-Q012.question: A life insurance beneficiary chooses a settlement option that guarantees a specified income for as long as he or she lives. However, the option states that if the beneficiary dies before the principal is completely exhausted, all payments stop and the remaining balance is forfeited to the insurer. Which option did you select?
options: Lifetime income with certain period
Fixed amount option
Pure Life Income Option
Interest only option
B07-Q012.explanation: The Straight Life Income option pays the highest monthly amount because it guarantees income for the beneficiary's entire life, but offers no guarantees beyond that. If the beneficiary dies shortly after payments begin, the insurer retains the remaining principal.

optionExplanations.Lifetime income with certain period: Lifetime Income with Certain Period guarantees payments for life, but also promises that if the beneficiary dies early, payments will continue to a secondary beneficiary for the remainder of the 'certain' period.
optionExplanations.Fixed amount option: The fixed amount option depletes the principal by paying a fixed dollar amount until the money runs out; It is not based on a life contingency.
optionExplanations.Interest only option: The interest-only option keeps the principal intact while paying only the interest earned.

B07-Q013.question: In the context of Social Security survivor benefits, the 'Blackout Period' is defined as the period during which survivor benefits are not paid to the surviving spouse. When does this specific period typically begin and end?
options: It begins immediately when the worker dies and ends 6 months later.
It begins when the youngest child turns 16 and ends when the surviving spouse turns 60.
It begins when the surviving spouse turns 50 and ends at full retirement age (65 or 67).
It begins when the youngest child turns 18 and ends when the surviving spouse turns 65.
B07-Q013.correctAnswer: It begins when the youngest child turns 16 and ends when the surviving spouse turns 60.
B07-Q013.explanation: Under Social Security rules, a surviving spouse who cares for dependent children receives benefits until the youngest child turns 16. After that, the spouse enters the 'Blackout Period', during which he or she does not receive survivor benefits until he or she qualifies for widow(er) retirement benefits, which can begin as early as age 60.

optionExplanations.It begins immediately when the worker di: There is no automatic 6-month blackout after the death of a worker; Eligible dependents begin receiving benefits almost immediately.
optionExplanations.It begins when the surviving spouse turn: Age 50 is relevant only if the surviving spouse is disabled, but does not define the standard blackout window.
optionExplanations.It begins when the youngest child turns: The cutoff for the parent's benefit is when the child turns 16, not 18 (although the child's own benefit continues until age 18), and spousal benefits can resume at age 60, not 65.

B07-Q018.question: A person looking to protect their retirement funds against market declines, while still participating in market growth, purchases an Equity-Indexed Annuity (EIA). How does an EIA achieve this balance?
options: Investing the premium directly in mutual funds, but absorbing any losses greater than 10%.
Guaranteeing a minimum interest rate floor to protect principal, while crediting additional interest based on the performance of a designated stock index.
Automatically moving all funds into bonds every time the stock index falls for three consecutive months.
Allowing the annuitant to personally select the individual stocks in which their funds are invested, ensuring they control risk.
B07-Q018.correctAnswer: Guaranteeing a minimum interest rate floor to protect principal, while crediting additional interest based on the performance of a designated stock index.
B07-Q018.explanation: Equity-Indexed Annuities are fixed annuities that provide a guaranteed minimum interest rate (the floor) that prevents loss of principal during market downturns. When the market performs well, they credit interest based on a formula linked to an external stock index (such as the S&P 500).

optionExplanations.Investing the premium directly in mutual: EIAs do not invest directly in mutual funds; That is a characteristic of Variable Annuities.
optionExplanations.Automatically moving all funds into bond: EIAs do not actively trade or move funds between bonds and stocks based on monthly performance.
optionExplanations.Allowing the annuitant to personally sel: Allowing the annuitant to choose individual shares or subaccounts is a feature of Variable Annuities, not EIAs.

B07-Q023.question: A beneficiary elects to leave a life insurance death benefit on deposit with the insurer under an interest-only settlement option. How are periodic amounts received by the beneficiary generally treated for federal income tax purposes?
options: Both the principal death benefit and interest payments are completely free of income tax.
The principal remains free of income tax, but the interest payments are taxable as ordinary income.
The entire series of payments is taxed as capital gains.
The entire series of payments is taxable as ordinary income because the beneficiary did not take a lump sum.
B07-Q023.correctAnswer: The principal remains free of income tax, but the interest payments are taxable as ordinary income.
B07-Q023.explanation: The principal of a life insurance death benefit is generally received free of income tax. However, when the beneficiary leaves the funds on deposit and receives interest-only payments, the interest portion is taxable as ordinary income.

optionExplanations.Both the principal death benefit and int: Only the principal of the death benefit is generally free of income tax; Interest earned after death is taxable.
optionExplanations.The entire series of payments is taxed a: Interest is not taxed as capital gain; They are generally taxed as ordinary income.
optionExplanations.The entire series of payments is taxable: The principal of the death benefit does not become taxable simply because the beneficiary elects an interest option; only the interest portion is taxable.

B07-Q020.question: A whole life insurance policy includes an Automatic Premium Loan provision and has enough cash value when the policyholder forgets to pay the annual premium. What will the insurer do if the policyholder does not take action before the grace period expires?
options: The policy will lapse immediately because the premium was not paid in cash.
The insurer will automatically pay the overdue premium through a policy loan against the cash value.
The insurer will convert the policy to reduced paid insurance without notice.
The insurer will cancel the policy and send the cash value to the policyholder.
B07-Q020.correctAnswer: The insurer will automatically pay the overdue premium through a policy loan against the cash value.
B07-Q020.explanation: Under an Automatic Premium Loan provision, if the policy has sufficient cash value and the premium is not paid at the end of the grace period, the insurer automatically advances the premium as a policy loan. This keeps the policy in force, with interest charged on the loan balance.

optionExplanations.The policy will lapse immediately becaus: If the policy includes an automatic premium loan provision and has sufficient cash value, the policy does not expire immediately at the end of the grace period.
optionExplanations.The insurer will convert the policy to r: Reduced paid insurance is a non-forfeiture option selected by the policyholder; This is not what the automatic premium loan provision does.
optionExplanations.The insurer will cancel the policy and s: The cash value is not automatically paid under an automatic premium loan provision; instead, it backs a policy loan to keep the policy active.

B07-Q021.question: A specialized consulting firm is owned by 5 equal partners. They decide to establish a Cross-Purchase Buy-Sell Agreement to ensure business continuity if one of the partners dies. How many separate life insurance policies must be purchased in total to fully fund this arrangement?
options: 5 policies
10 policies
20 policies
25 policies
B07-Q021.explanation: In a Cross-Purchase Buy-Sell Agreement, each partner must purchase a policy on each of the other partners. The formula to determine the total number of policies required is N x (N - 1), where N is the number of partners. With 5 partners: 5 x (5 - 1) = 5 x 4 = 20 policies.

optionExplanations.5 policies: 5 policies would be required under an Entity Purchase plan, where the company itself purchases a policy on each partner.
optionExplanations.10 policies: 10 is an arbitrary number and does not fit the Cross-Purchase formula.
optionExplanations.25 policies: 25 would be N x N, which includes each partner purchasing a policy on themselves, which defeats the purpose of the agreement.

B07-Q019.question: An insured has a basic medical expenses policy and a supplemental Major Medical policy. After the basic policy exhausts its limits, the insured must pay a specific out-of-pocket amount before the supplemental policy begins to pay. What is this specific deductible called?
options: A fixed deductible
A broker deductible
A built-in deductible
A maximum out-of-pocket deductible
B07-Q019.explanation: A corridor deductible applies to Major Medical supplement plans. It functions as a 'broker' bridging the gap between the exhaustion of Basic Medical Plan benefits and the initiation of Major Medical supplemental coverage.

optionExplanations.A fixed deductible: A fixed deductible is a fixed dollar amount applied at the beginning of a claim, typical of comprehensive Major Medical plans.
optionExplanations.A built-in deductible: A built-in deductible means that the amount paid for the basic plan counts toward satisfying Major Medical's deductible.
optionExplanations.A maximum out-of-pocket deductible: Out-of-pocket maximum refers to the stop-loss limit, not the bridging deductible between basic and supplemental plans.

B07-Q024.question: Under the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), if an insurance company denies a request based on information obtained from an investigative consumer report, the insurer is legally required to:
options: Provide the applicant with a free copy of the full report within 3 days.
Provide the requester with the name and address of the consumer reporting agency that provided the report.
Destroy all records of the application to protect consumer privacy.
Offer the applicant a high-risk policy alternative before issuing a formal denial.
B07-Q024.correctAnswer: Provide the requester with the name and address of the consumer reporting agency that provided the report.
B07-Q024.explanation: If adverse action (such as a denial) is taken based on a consumer report, the Fair Credit Reporting Act requires the user of the report (the insurer) to provide the requester with the name, address, and telephone number of the reporting agency that provided the information, so that the consumer can verify or dispute the findings.

optionExplanations.Provide the applicant with a free copy o: The insurer does not provide the copy of the report; The consumer must request the copy directly from the reporting agency.
optionExplanations.Destroy all records of the application t: Insurers must retain records to demonstrate compliance and justify underwriting decisions; They don't destroy them.
optionExplanations.Offer the applicant a high-risk policy a: The FCRA regulates privacy and disclosure, not underwriting decisions. Insurers are not required to offer alternative policies.

B08-Q001.question: For an Annually Renewable Term (ART) life insurance policy, what happens to the premium and death benefit each year upon renewal?
options: The premium remains level, but the death benefit decreases.
Both the premium and the death benefit increase.
The premium increases based on the insured's attained age, while the death benefit remains level.
The premium decreases based on favorable mortality experience, while the death benefit remains level.
B08-Q001.correctAnswer: The premium increases based on the insured's attained age, while the death benefit remains level.
B08-Q001.explanation: Annually Renewable Term (ART) insurance provides a level death benefit for a period of one year. When the policy is renewed each year without evidence of insurability, the premium increases because it is recalculated based on the older reached age of the insured.

optionExplanations.The premium remains level, but the death: This describes a level-premium decreasing term policy, often used for mortgage protection.
optionExplanations.Both the premium and the death benefit i: The death benefit does not automatically increase in a standard ART policy.
optionExplanations.The premium decreases based on favorable: Premiums increase as the insured ages, reflecting the increased statistical risk of death; they do not decrease.

B08-Q002.question: A father purchases a life insurance policy on his minor child and includes a Payer Benefit rider. If the parent dies or becomes totally disabled before the child reaches the age of majority, what does this rider expressly provide?
options: Immediately pays the death benefit to the child.
Waives payment of premiums until the child reaches a specific age, usually 21 years old.
Doubles the face amount of the policy.
Transfers ownership of the policy to a court-appointed guardian.
B08-Q002.correctAnswer: Waives payment of premiums until the child reaches a specific age, usually 21 years old.
B08-Q002.explanation: The Payer Benefit rider is commonly attached to youth policies. If the adult premium payer (usually a parent) dies or becomes totally disabled, the insurer waives premiums until the insured child reaches a specific age, such as 21, ensuring that the policy does not lapse.

optionExplanations.Immediately pays the death benefit to th: The policy insures the child, not the father. The death of the father does not activate the death benefit.
This additional clause waives premiums; does not increase the nominal amount.
optionExplanations.Transfers ownership of the policy to a c: Although ownership could be legally transferred, the specific financial function of the payer benefit rider is premium waiver, not ownership management.

B08-Q004.question: An employer pays the entire premium for a group term life insurance policy covering its employees. Under federal tax law, how is the cost of this coverage to the employee treated?
options: The entire premium paid by the employer is tax-free to the employee.
The entire premium paid by the employer is treated as taxable ordinary income for the employee.
The cost of the first $50,000 of coverage is tax-free, but the cost of coverage that exceeds $50,000 is treated as taxable imputed income.
Premiums are tax-free, but the death benefit will be fully taxable to the employee's beneficiary.
B08-Q004.correctAnswer: The cost of the first $50,000 of coverage is tax-free, but the cost of coverage that exceeds $50,000 is treated as taxable imputed income.
B08-Q004.explanation: Under Section 79 of the Internal Revenue Code, the cost of employer-provided group term life insurance up to $50,000 is tax-free to the employee. The cost of any coverage amount provided over $50,000 is considered a taxable fringe benefit and is treated as imputed income to the employee.

optionExplanations.The entire premium paid by the employer: The exemption is strictly limited to $50,000 of coverage. Higher amounts generate taxable income.
Only the value of coverage that exceeds $50,000 generates taxable income, not the entire premium.
optionExplanations.Premiums are tax-free, but the death ben: Death benefits from employer-sponsored group term life insurance are generally received income tax free by the beneficiary, just as with individual life insurance.

B08-Q010.question: A wealthy person dies, and his or her life insurance death benefits are included in his or her gross estate, subjecting the proceeds to federal estate taxes. Which of the following scenarios is the main reason why this inclusion would occur?
options: The death benefit exceeded the IRS annual gift tax exclusion limit.
The insured had “incidents of ownership” on the policy at the time of his death.
The policy was classified as a Modified Endowment Contract (MEC).
The beneficiary elected to receive the death benefit in a lump sum.
B08-Q010.correctAnswer: The insured had “incidents of ownership” on the policy at the time of his death.
B08-Q010.explanation: Life insurance proceeds are included in the decedent's gross estate for federal estate tax purposes if the proceeds are payable to the estate, or if the decedent had any “incident of ownership” in the policy at the time of his or her death (such as the right to change the beneficiary, borrow against the cash value, or assign the policy).

optionExplanations.The death benefit exceeded the IRS annua: The gift tax exclusion limit applies to living gifts (such as paying premiums for another person), not to the inclusion of death benefits in an estate.
optionExplanations.The policy was classified as a Modified: MEC status alters the taxation of living benefits (loans/withdrawals), but does not cause death benefits to be subject to estate taxes.
optionExplanations.The beneficiary elected to receive the d: Lump-sum death benefits are generally income tax-free. The liquidation option does not determine inclusion in equity; ownership yes.

B08-Q008.question: A policyholder names an irrevocable beneficiary on a life insurance policy. Which of the following rights does the policyholder lose as a direct result of this specific designation?
options: The right to pay policy premiums.
The right to change the beneficiary, borrow against the cash value, or assign the policy without the beneficiary's consent.
The right to receive dividends from the policy.
The right to let the policy lapse due to non-payment.
B08-Q008.correctAnswer: The right to change the beneficiary, borrow against the cash value, or assign the policy without the beneficiary's consent.
B08-Q008.explanation: Naming an irrevocable beneficiary gives that beneficiary a vested interest in the policy. The policyholder loses the right to unilaterally alter the policy, such as changing the beneficiary, taking a loan from the policy, or assigning the contract, without obtaining the written consent of the irrevocable beneficiary.

The policyholder retains the right and obligation to pay premiums.
optionExplanations.The right to receive dividends from the: Dividend options are generally selected by the holder unless they affect the guaranteed cash value or death benefit in a way that harms the interest of the irrevocable beneficiary.
optionExplanations.The right to let the policy lapse due to: The policyholder can still let the policy lapse by failing to pay premiums; The beneficiary cannot force the owner to pay.

B08-Q007.question: Under the Uniform Individual Accident and Illness Policy Provisions Act, an insurer must provide claim forms within 15 days after receiving a notice of claim. If the insurer does not provide the forms within that time frame, how can the insured legally comply with the proof of loss requirement?
options: Verbally describing the loss to the agent over the phone.
Waiting indefinitely until the insurer eventually sends out the official forms.
Submitting written proof detailing the occurrence, character and extent of the loss within the required time frame.
The insured is permanently exempt from proving the loss and the claim must be paid automatically.
B08-Q007.correctAnswer: Submitting written proof detailing the occurrence, character and extent of the loss within the required time frame.
B08-Q007.explanation: Under the Claim Forms provision, if the insurer does not provide the necessary forms within 15 days after being notified, the claimant is deemed to have met the proof of loss requirement by submitting its own written proof detailing the nature and extent of the loss within the time period specified in the policy.

optionExplanations.Verbally describing the loss to the agen: A verbal description is insufficient; The claimant must present written proof.
optionExplanations.Waiting indefinitely until the insurer e: The insured is not protected if he simply waits; You must still submit written proof within the original proof of loss period (typically 90 days).
optionExplanations.The insured is permanently exempt from p: Failure to submit forms by the insurer does not guarantee automatic payment; The insured still has the legal burden of providing written evidence of the loss.

B08-Q005.question: An agent is reviewing a completed life insurance application with an applicant and notices an error in the medical history section. What is the proper procedure to correct this error?
options: The agent must use whiteout to hide the error and write the correct information.
The agent should cross out the error, write the correct information, and have the requester initial the change.
The agent must submit the application as is and attach a separate explanatory note to the subscriber.
The agent must delete the error, correct it independently, and sign their own name next to the change.
B08-Q005.correctAnswer: The agent should cross out the error, write the correct information, and have the requester initial the change.
B08-Q005.explanation: If an error is made on an insurance application, the proper procedure is to cross out the error, write the correct information, and have the applicant initial the change to verify that he or she acknowledges and accepts the correction.

optionExplanations.The agent must use whiteout to hide the: White-out should never be used on an application, as it involves manipulation or concealment of information.
optionExplanations.The agent must submit the application as: Leaving a known error on the application form creates legal liability, even with a note attached.
optionExplanations.The agent must delete the error, correct: Agents cannot independently alter the requester's responses. The applicant must authorize and initial any changes.

B08-Q011.question: A manufacturing company is structured as a partnership with four equal partners. To finance an Entity Purchase or Stock Redemption agreement, how many life insurance policies must be purchased in total?
options: 4 policies
8 policies
12 policies
16 policies
B08-Q011.explanation: In an Entity Purchase or Stock Redemption agreement, the business entity purchases, owns, and pays the premiums on a policy for each partner. With four partners, the company simply purchases 4 policies. (This is in contrast to a cross-purchase plan, which would require 12 policies.)

optionExplanations.8 policies: 8 is mathematically incorrect for both types of plans.
optionExplanations.12 policies: 12 policies would be required under a cross-purchase plan, where each partner purchases one policy on each of the other partners using the N x (N - 1) formula.
optionExplanations.16 policies: 16 is mathematically incorrect and would represent N x N, which includes partners purchasing policies on themselves.

B08-Q012.question: The mandatory Complete Contract provision in a life insurance policy stipulates that the policy document and a copy of the original application constitute the complete contract. Under this provision, who is expressly prohibited from making changes to the policy or waiving any of its provisions?
options: The president of the insurance company
An executive officer of the insurance company
The insurance agent
The main beneficiary
B08-Q012.explanation: The Entire Contract provision states that only an executive officer of the insurance company can make changes to the contract. It expressly states that an agent has no authority to alter the contract or waive any of its provisions.

optionExplanations.The president of the insurance company: The president of the insurance company is an executive officer and typically has legal authority to approve changes.
optionExplanations.An executive officer of the insurance co: Executive officers are specifically authorized to approve contractual amendments.
optionExplanations.The main beneficiary: Although a beneficiary cannot change the contract, the provision exists specifically to clarify the limits of the agent's authority to bind the insurer.

B08-Q013.question: In an individual disability income policy, what does the “benefit period” represent?
options: The length of time the insured must wait before benefits begin.
The maximum duration for which the policy will pay disability benefits for a continuous period of disability.
The period during which the policyholder can renew the contract.
The number of days an insured has to submit formal proof of loss.
B08-Q013.correctAnswer: The maximum duration for which the policy will pay disability benefits for a continuous period of disability.
B08-Q013.explanation: The benefit period in a disability income policy is the maximum amount of time (for example, 2 years, 5 years, or up to age 65) during which the insurer will pay income benefits for a covered disability. A longer benefit period results in a higher premium.

optionExplanations.The length of time the insured must wait: The time the insured must wait before benefits begin is known as the elimination period or waiting period.
optionExplanations.The period during which the policyholder: This relates to renewability provisions (such as guaranteed renewable or non-cancelable), not the benefit period.
optionExplanations.The number of days an insured has to sub: The deadline for submitting proof of loss is a standard claims provision (typically 90 days), not the benefit period.

B08-Q015.question: A policyholder stops paying premiums on a whole life policy and elects the “Reduced Paid-Up” non-lapse option. How will the policy coverage change?
options: The face amount remains the same, but the coverage becomes temporary insurance and will eventually expire.
The cash value acts as a single premium to purchase a fully paid whole life policy with a lower death benefit.
The insurer uses the cash value to automatically pay the existing premium until the cash value is depleted.
The policy is cancelled, and the cash value is paid as a single lump sum to the policyholder.
B08-Q015.correctAnswer: The cash value acts as a single premium to purchase a fully paid whole life policy with a lower death benefit.
B08-Q015.explanation: Under the Reduced Paid-Up non-lapse option, the insurer uses the accumulated cash value of the policy as a single net premium to purchase a fully paid permanent (whole life) policy. The new policy covers the insured for life, but at a reduced face amount compared to the original policy.

optionExplanations.The face amount remains the same, but th: This describes the extended term insurance non-lapse option.
optionExplanations.The insurer uses the cash value to autom: This describes the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) provision, not a non-forfeiture option.
optionExplanations.The policy is cancelled, and the cash va: This describes the Cash Surrender nonforfeiture option.

B08-Q017.question: Under the Uniform Individual Accident and Sickness Policy Provisions Act, after written proof of loss has been presented, how long must an insured generally wait before taking legal action against the insurer?
options: 30 days
45 days
60 days
90 days
B08-Q017.explanation: The Legal Actions provision generally prohibits a lawsuit until 60 days after written proof of loss has been presented and also limits the lawsuit to within three years after proof of loss is required.

optionExplanations.30 days: Thirty days is not the standard waiting period before suing under the legal action provision.
optionExplanations.45 days: Forty-five days is associated with certain clear claims deadlines, not the waiting period for legal action.
optionExplanations.90 days: Ninety days is commonly associated with submitting proof of loss, not the waiting period before filing a lawsuit.
